transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jamal Reed (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Redwood Partner Ops), Priya Kapoor (LumenWorks Head of Partnerships), Ethan Cole (LumenWorks Enterprise Sales Dir), Maya Lin (LumenWorks SA), Omar Ruiz (Channel Ops)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
High-level: Align on co-sell pipeline, pick 3 pilot accounts, agree on rev-share and pricing, schedule benchmarks. Security checklist needed: SOC2 report, SSO/SAML docs, KMS integration notes, VPC/private deployment options.

[00:00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. Quick intros for anyone new — I'm Ava, AE on the Redwood partner team.
[00:00:09] Priya Kapoor: Hi all — Priya here, leading partnerships at LumenWorks. We've got Ethan and Maya, and Omar on for ops.
[00:00:16] Ethan Cole: Hey, yeah thanks.
[00:00:18] Jamal Reed: Jamal from Redwood SE — I'll drive the tech bits and the bench planning.
[00:00:24] Maya Lin: Maya, solutions at LumenWorks.
[00:00:28] Ava Martinez: Great. Agenda — quick pipeline review, pick pilot accounts, pricing/rev-share discussion, bench scope and timelines, security asks, and next steps. Does that work?
[00:00:38] Priya Kapoor: Yep, perfect.

[00:02:10] Ava Martinez: I'll start with the pipeline — from our end we see three mutual accounts that look promising: Northbridge Health, Atlas Fleet, and ClearHarbor Finance. These match the verticals LumenWorks is focused on — healthcare, logistics, and fintech. We think a 3-account pilot is pragmatic to show value and surface any infra/security asks early.
[00:02:35] Ethan Cole: Northbridge is huge for us, we've got an exec sponsor there. Atlas Fleet is a greenfield motion though — they'd be interested in automating dispatch and claims triage. ClearHarbor is more security-sensitive, probably will push for VPC or private deployment.
[00:02:52] Ava Martinez: Totally — ClearHarbor will be the canary for security. For that one we should plan for either Redwood Dedicated or our Private offering. Jamal — will a dedicated pool suffice for initial bench?
[00:03:05] Jamal Reed: Yeah Dedicated should be fine for benchmarking latency and throughput. We can also reproduce a VPC-like environment for network constraints. Note though, some wp-words — I mean, some customers push for on-prem, which adds lead time.
[00:03:20] Maya Lin: How long is lead time for Private?
[00:03:24] Jamal Reed: Private deployment tends to be a few weeks to a couple months depending on compliance reviews and KMS/HSM integration. Dedicated is faster — usually days to spin up reserved capacity after contract.

[00:05:12] Priya Kapoor: On rev-share, LumenWorks typically asks for a market development fund or a 10-20% rev-share for initial introductions, depending on deal size. What does Redwood usually do?
[00:05:25] Ava Martinez: We have flexibility for pilots; standard co-sell pilot terms we've done recently are a modest discount + 10% co-sell commission for active pipeline-sourced deals. For larger enterprise bookings we can discuss tiered splits. We'll send a formal addendum.
[00:05:38] Omar Ruiz: And how about credits for the bench? If you're running extensive benchmarks that drive cost, is that billable?
[00:05:45] Jamal Reed: For a 1-2 day benchmark we usually absorb the infra cost if it's a joint pilot. If it's multi-week continuous testing with big data sets, we'll put a cap or recommend a short-term dev bundle. We'll outline options in the addendum.

[00:07:50] Ethan Cole: One pushback we hear: latency vs cost — customers want sub-200ms for chat but are sensitive to token costs. Can you explain Redwood's levers?
[00:08:02] Ava Martinez: Sure — there are trade-offs. We recommend Dedicated for latency-sensitive apps; batching and KV caching reduce per-token cost but impact tail latency trade-offs. Also quantized model variants can reduce cost but sometimes affect quality. Our Optimize team can recommend per-workload profiles.
[00:08:18] Priya Kapoor: Do you have docs we can share with their engineering teams about those trade-offs?
[00:08:22] Ava Martinez: Yes — we'll share the Optimize recommendations deck and a short one-pager on latency/cost levers.

[00:10:40] Maya Lin: For ClearHarbor, they will need SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML integration, KMS for keys, and detailed audit logs. Will you be able to provide those?
[00:10:51] Jamal Reed: We have SOC 2 and ISO notes; for KMS we support customer-managed keys integrations; audit logs and RBAC are available in the console. I'll attach the security pack.
[00:11:05] Maya Lin: Great, we need that before any formal intro.

[00:13:30] Ava Martinez: Ok, bench plan — Jamal, can you outline the benchmark scope and what we need from LumenWorks and the customer?
[00:13:39] Jamal Reed: Sure. Scope: three short tests — (1) latency at 1:1 and 10:1 concurrency for typical prompts, (2) throughput and token cost per 1k tokens, (3) quality check vs current baseline for extraction tasks. We need representative prompt sets, sample payload sizes, and an account-specific SLA target — like p95 under 300ms for chat. Also we need an agreed dataset and success criteria.
[00:14:05] Priya Kapoor: We'll pull sample prompts from Northbridge and Atlas. For ClearHarbor we'll share a sanitized set.
[00:14:12] Jamal Reed: Perfect. We'll also provide the bench script and a spreadsheet for results (I'll call it benchmark_spreadsheet_v1 — link to be shared).

[00:17:00] Ethan Cole: On pricing, can you give a ballpark for the pilot? We usually try to sell pilot as a paid POC with ability to convert credits.
[00:17:09] Ava Martinez: Ballpark: for small pilots of 3 accounts and limited traffic, we're looking at $12k- $30k for a 3-month pilot depending on model usage and dedicated vs hosted. We'll firm up numbers once we know traffic and model selection. We'll send a pricing addendum.
[00:17:27] Priya Kapoor: That aligns with our expectations. If we co-sell and we bring the account in, what's the typical T&Cs for lead credit?
[00:17:36] Ava Martinez: We document introductions in the co-sell addendum and provide partner credit and tracking in the partner portal. Lena, can you confirm the tracking cadence?
[00:17:43] Lena Cho: Yep — we'll enable shared pipeline view in the portal and set weekly syncs. We'll also log deal owner and source.

[00:20:10] Maya Lin: For the bench, we might need a small private dataset for ClearHarbor to simulate PII. Can Redwood sign an NDA around that?
[00:20:18] Jamal Reed: Yes, we can work under a mutual NDA and handle any sensitive tokens carefully. For datasets we can also run in a customer-managed VPC so data never leaves their network.

[00:25:00] Priya Kapoor: One other question — integration with LumenWorks' platform: we typically do a joint solution that bundles LumenWorks orchestration with Redwood inference. Any gotchas around SDKs or latency when integrating?
[00:25:12] Jamal Reed: We expose REST and SDK clients; latency is mostly network and model choice. If you're embedding in LumenWorks runtime we recommend edge routing and using regional endpoints. Also watch for KV cache warming if you have many cold starts — that can create a small spike.
[00:25:32] Ethan Cole: Do you have reference architectures for co-sell integrations?
[00:25:36] Ava Martinez: Yes — we'll share a reference architecture diagram in the deck.

[00:30:05] Ava Martinez: Let's pick the three pilot accounts today — do we have agreement on Northbridge, Atlas, and ClearHarbor?
[00:30:12] Priya Kapoor: Yes, those three. We'll prioritize Northbridge as the opener.
[00:30:18] Ethan Cole: Agreed. Northbridge has the executive sponsor and a 60-90 day timeline.
[00:30:24] Ava Martinez: Great. Action items: LumenWorks share account champions and basic SOW asks; Redwood to send co-sell deck, pricing addendum, and bench script.

[00:35:45] Omar Ruiz: On the partner portal, can we get visibility into lead stage and ARR estimate?
[00:35:52] Lena Cho: Yes — we'll enable ARR estimate field and a shared comment thread per deal.

[00:40:00] Priya Kapoor: Any blockers from Redwood's side to start the Northbridge intro?
[00:40:07] Ava Martinez: We'll need the intro email and confirmation that Northbridge is ok with Redwood being looped in. Also the security checklist for ClearHarbor must be acknowledged. Otherwise we can start enablement.

[00:45:30] Jamal Reed: For bench scheduling — would Oct 21 work for a focused 3-4 hour run? We can run tests and debrief same day.
[00:45:37] Priya Kapoor: Oct 21 is good. I'll confirm with the Northbridge team and get back.

[00:50:00] Ava Martinez: Recap and next steps — we'll: (1) send co-sell deck and reference architecture (Ava) by 10/17, (2) send pricing addendum and pilot rev-share proposal (Ava) by 10/18, (3) Jamal to share bench script and schedule 10/21 target, (4) Priya to send prioritized accounts and champions by 10/18, (5) Lena to enable portal access and shared pipeline by 10/19.
[00:50:28] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
[00:50:32] Ethan Cole: Thanks.
[00:50:34] Maya Lin: Thanks all.
[00:50:36] Ava Martinez: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the deck and benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:50:44] Meeting end.
